t: More prompts improve readability but can make the world feel like a checklist.
Hold prompts should be reserved for destructive, costly, or long-duration interactions.
a: Support text scaling, remapped glyphs, hold/toggle alternatives, and high-contrast prompt backgrounds.
Do not rely only on proximity; combine world highlight, text, and prompt positioning where possible.

ui_ux.inventory_grid.d: A slot-based interface for viewing, moving, stacking, sorting, equipping, or using items.
e: Full inventory, partial stacks, locked slots, quest items, and equipment restrictions need clear feedback.
Controller focus should not get trapped when filtered views hide the currently selected item.
Drag/drop must define what happens when the target slot becomes invalid during multiplayer or sorting updates.
b: Client UI moves an item before server validation and duplicates or loses it after correction.
Sorting changes item indices while a tooltip or drag operation still references the old slot.
Stack splitting allows zero, negative, or over-cap quantities.
t: Small grids create meaningful scarcity but can make loot-heavy games feel like inventory work.
Sorting and filtering reduce friction without necessarily increasing carrying capacity.
a: Support text scaling, high-contrast rarity indicators, gamepad focus order, and non-drag alternatives.
Do not rely only on item icon art; include names, categories, and comparison text where possible.

ui_ux.minimap.d: A small persistent map view that summarizes nearby terrain, objectives, entities, or navigation context.
e: Multi-floor spaces need above/below or floor selection cues.
Procedural maps need stable icon and reveal behavior across seed regeneration.
Too many icons can hide the player arrow or objective marker.
b: Rotating minimap text and icons become unreadable because they rotate with terrain.
Fog reveal state updates visually but not in saved map data.
Entity icons continue showing after despawn or stealth state changes.
t: Showing enemies and loot increases efficiency but can reduce exploration and surprise.
North-up maps support geographic learning; rotating maps support immediate turn-by-turn navigation.
a: Provide size, opacity, icon filtering, and colorblind-safe icon shapes.
Avoid making minimap reading mandatory when landmarks, compass cues, or objective text could also guide players.

ui_ux.quest_marker.d: An objective-state projection that maps quest, mission, or task targets into world, map, compass, or screen-space markers with priority and visibility rules.
e: Objectives inside caves, buildings, or stacked floors need vertical and pathing cues, not only straight-line direction.
Multiple active quests can flood the HUD unless filtered or prioritized.
Moving objectives and NPCs need marker smoothing without lying about position.
b: Marker points to world origin after the quest target despawns.
Straight-line distance sends players toward cliffs or locked doors without context.
Completed markers remain on compass because quest state and marker state update in different systems.
t: Exact markers reduce friction but can remove exploration and environmental reading.
Area markers preserve mystery while still giving players enough direction to proceed.
a: Use shape, text, and distance labels in addition to color, and provide marker size/opacity settings.
Allow players to reduce marker clutter or pin only one objective at a time.

ui_ux.radial_menu.d: A circular selection UI that lets players choose tools, weapons, commands, or abilities by direction.
e: Empty or locked slices should communicate why they cannot be selected.
Very small stick movement, mouse jitter, and touch release near boundaries need stable selection rules.
Opening the menu during reload, dialogue, pause, or multiplayer combat must define whether time changes.
b: Release commits the previous slice because highlight updates after input release.
Stick deadzone differs from gameplay movement and causes accidental selections.
Time scale affects networked gameplay or UI animation unexpectedly.
t: Time slowdown makes selection easier but reduces pressure; real-time wheels preserve risk.
A radial menu should usually contain few high-frequency choices rather than every item in the game.
a: Offer hold/toggle open behavior, remapping, larger labels, and non-radial list alternatives.
Avoid requiring precise analog direction for critical actions without confirmation or deadzone tuning.

ui_ux.tutorial_prompt.d: A contextual UI hint that teaches controls, rules, or next steps when the player is likely to need them.
e: Prompts should update immediately when input device or bindings change.
A prompt during combat, dialogue, or cutscene can obscure urgent information.
Dismissed prompts may need to return after long absence, repeated failure, or changed control scheme.
b: Prompt appears after the player has already completed the taught action.
Dismissal state is saved globally and hides the prompt for new save files.
Input glyphs show default bindings instead of remapped controls.
t: Hints should reduce confusion, not solve puzzles or remove discovery unless the game opts into guided play.
Failure-based prompts are often less intrusive than showing every instruction preemptively.
a: Allow prompt duration, size, and repeat behavior to be adjusted.
Use text plus icons, and ensure prompts are compatible with screen reader or narration systems where supported.

vehicles.drifting.d: A vehicle intentionally exceeds normal tire grip and slides through a turn while retaining steerable control.
e: The vehicle starts drifting while airborne or with partial wheel contact.
A collision occurs during drift and should cancel, preserve, or convert drift charge.
Surface changes mid-corner and grip recovery becomes abrupt.
b: Drift state toggles rapidly around the threshold and flickers camera, score, or boost UI.
Countersteer assist fights player input and prevents intentional spin recovery.
Drift charge continues while sliding backward or scraping a wall.
t: If drifting grants boost, normal cornering still needs a reason to exist on some track shapes.
Higher assist improves accessibility but can flatten mastery unless optional or difficulty-scaled.
a: Offer steer assist, reduced camera yaw, and optional drift automation for players who struggle with counter-steering.
Use visual, audio, and controller cues to indicate drift state without relying only on tire smoke.

vehicles.fuel.d: A vehicle consumes a stored resource while driving, boosting, idling, or powering systems, and changes behavior when depleted.
e: The driver exits or disconnects during a refuel transaction.
Fuel reaches zero while the vehicle is airborne, on a slope, or crossing a checkpoint.
A damaged fuel tank leaks while UI range estimates still assume normal capacity.
b: Fuel drains from render delta and depends on frame rate.
Refuel items are consumed twice after retrying a failed network request.
Save/load restores vehicle position but resets fuel to full or empty.
t: Fuel pressure works best when refueling routes and fallback travel are readable.
Open-world fuel scarcity can create memorable planning, but it should not strand players without recovery options.
a: Show fuel warnings with text, icons, and route estimates rather than a tiny gauge only.
Allow relaxed fuel consumption or assist settings in exploration-focused modes.

vehicles.suspension_physics.d: A vehicle handling model where wheels or hover points compress against terrain, transferring contact information into ride height, grip, stability, and body roll.
p: wheel_contact_state: per wheel: grounded, compression, normal, slip
e: Only one wheel remains grounded on a curb or rock and the chassis receives a large roll impulse.
A vehicle lands from a jump with wheel contacts appearing over several physics steps instead of all at once.
Terrain triangles produce rapidly changing contact normals at road mesh seams.
b: Wheel contact rays start inside the ground after large bumps, causing sudden launch impulses.
Damping is applied with frame delta instead of fixed-step delta and produces platform-dependent bounce.
Surface material changes update tire effects but not grip, making mud or ice look correct but drive like asphalt.
t: Higher stiffness improves steering precision but can make rough terrain unreadable and punishing.
More damping reduces bounce after jumps but can make the vehicle feel heavy and unresponsive.
a: Offer camera shake and roll reduction for players sensitive to suspension-driven body motion.
Provide steering assist or stability assist presets when uneven terrain demands rapid correction.

vehicles.upgradeable_vehicle.d: A progression system where players install compatible vehicle parts that change handling, durability, utility, storage, fuel use, or traversal capability.
p: vehicle_id: stable vehicle archetype or instance id
compatibility_rule_id: per vehicle family or slot group
e: A content update removes or renames an installed upgrade_part_id in an existing save.
The player previews an upgrade while another menu, teammate, or server request changes the same vehicle.
A part install would exceed storage capacity because removed parts need to return to inventory.
b: The UI preview uses client-only formulas that do not match the authoritative stat modifier pipeline.
Installed parts duplicate when an equip operation succeeds but inventory removal fails.
Vehicle physics caches are not rebuilt after part changes, so new handling appears only after reload.
t: Purely dominant parts collapse build variety; attach tradeoffs to mass, grip, durability, storage, or fuel use.
Upgrade availability can pace world traversal, but hard-gating too many routes can make vehicles feel like keys instead of tools.
a: Expose upgrade effects in text as well as bars or icons, especially for color-dependent comparisons.
Let players compare current, previewed, and previous configurations without relying on memory.

vehicles.vehicle_acceleration.d: A vehicle converts driver throttle input into forward motion through engine, traction, surface, and authority rules.
e: Throttle is held while the vehicle is airborne, upside down, or missing wheel contact.
Surface changes from asphalt to mud during the same fixed step that acceleration is applied.
Client prediction applies throttle but the server rejects driver ownership after a seat swap.
b: Acceleration is integrated from render delta and changes with frame rate.
Throttle input remains latched after driver disconnect, pause, or seat exit.
Traction modifiers are applied after velocity cap, making mud affect launch but not top pace.
t: Strong launch acceleration feels responsive but can make tight tracks or combat encounters hard to read.
Surface traction should change route choices without making vehicles feel randomly underpowered.
a: Offer throttle assist, input smoothing, or digital trigger support for players without analog controls.
Provide camera options that reduce sudden pitch or acceleration shake.

vehicles.vehicle_boost.d: A temporary vehicle power state that converts a stored meter, pickup, drift reward, or scripted trigger into extra acceleration and stronger audiovisual emphasis.
e: Boost activates while the vehicle is airborne and should not produce impossible steering correction.
A boost pickup is collected on the same server tick as meter activation.
The vehicle hits a wall during the burst and needs damage, camera, and meter state resolved in order.
b: Boost meter is deducted twice when activation and pickup collection arrive in the same update.
Camera field of view remains widened after interruption, respawn, or vehicle swap.
Boost acceleration ignores surface traction and makes ice, mud, and ramps behave like flat asphalt.
t: Short bursts reward timing; long bursts become route-planning resources and need stronger counterplay from turns or hazards.
Recharge rules determine behavior: drift charging encourages risky cornering, pickup charging encourages track control, and passive recharge reduces pressure.
a: Offer reduced camera push, reduced shake, and lower audio spike settings for boost feedback.
Make boost meter state readable through shape, text, or placement rather than color alone.

vehicles.vehicle_braking.d: A vehicle reduces velocity, reverses, or locks traction according to brake input, surface grip, and wheel state.
e: Brake input is held while the vehicle is airborne or has only one wheel touching ground.
The player switches from reverse to forward throttle while sliding downhill.
Handbrake input overlaps with drift scoring, boost cancellation, or damage-induced wheel loss.
b: Braking applies a direct velocity clamp and ignores traction, causing instant stops on ice.
Reverse engages while the vehicle is still moving forward too quickly.
Handbrake state remains active after seat exit or input device disconnect.
t: Short stopping distances improve accessibility but reduce racing line skill.
Handbrakes should be useful for tight turns without becoming faster than normal cornering everywhere.
a: Offer braking assist or auto-brake options for players who struggle with analog timing.
Keep camera shake and skid audio adjustable during heavy braking.

vehicles.vehicle_damage.d: A vehicle durability model where collisions, weapons, terrain hazards, or misuse reduce whole-vehicle or part-specific health and can affect handling, visuals, and repair needs.
e: A vehicle receives several contact impulses in one physics step and should not apply duplicate damage for one crash.
A player exits or swaps seats while the vehicle transitions from damaged to disabled.
A repaired vehicle still has old smoke, tire, or dent presentation attached to pooled objects.
b: Damage uses raw velocity difference instead of resolved collision impulse, causing harmless scrapes to destroy vehicles.
Part health reaches zero but drivetrain, steering, or wheel constraints continue as if intact.
Repair consumes materials client-side before the server accepts the repair transaction.
t: Pure handling penalties can make recovery frustrating; reserve severe penalties for readable impacts or optional simulation modes.
Repair costs should scale with route risk and economy pacing, not punish small cosmetic mistakes excessively.
a: Show damage state through text, icons, sound, and visual stages so it is not dependent on subtle deformation.
Offer reduced handling penalty or assisted recovery options for players who struggle with damaged steering.
